subject: Session-index purge checklist, keystore residency proof, and SOC 2 evidence request
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@mednexa.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: GRC Team <grc@mednexa.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Session-index purge checklist, keystore residency & SOC 2 artifacts

Hi Priyom,

We're updating our SIG/CAIQ pack ahead of a customer audit and have a few follow-ups specific to Redwood's session and ephemeral telemetry lifecycle. Please help with the items below so we can complete the evidence bundle for our auditors:

1) Session-index / session-id retention: Your docs say session metadata expires at 30 days by default. For the customers on dedicated or private deployments, can you produce:
   - a deletion manifest sample showing the record IDs removed, timestamp, and controller who initiated the purge;
   - the policy that drives TTL vs manual purge;

2) Ephemeral KV-cache traces: We need to understand how long KV cache items (model key/value shards used to accelerate inference) are retained and how they are destroyed. Specifically:
   - confirmation of in-memory eviction vs persisted tombstone deletion;
   - any off-host traces (e.g., debug logs) that may contain cache identifiers and where those logs are stored;

3) Keystore residency & rotation evidence: For customer-managed keys (CMKs) used to encrypt session-export artifacts, please provide the keystore residency statement (region, cloud provider), key rotation logs for the last 90 days, and the doc describing key rotation procedure.

4) SOC 2 / CAIQ artifacts: We need a concise list of the artifacts Redwood can provide (signed attestation, sample manifests, S3 proof-of-delete records, CloudTrail snippets, SOC 2 mapping rows) and a suggested delivery timeline. Our deadline for the evidence handoff to auditors is Dec 14.

Can you respond with a short checklist and sample artifacts (redacted as needed)? If it helps, we can take a 30-minute technical call this week.

Thanks —
Elena Ruiz
Head of Security, MedNexa
elena.ruiz@mednexa.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Elena —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short checklist and our keystore residency matrix to start (see attachments). Quick summary here so your GRC team can triage:

- Deletion manifests: we can provide redacted JSON manifests (sample attached: engineer-deletion-manifest-sample.json) that show object ids, deletion timestamps, and the purge job id. For Dedicated customers we can also provide tenant-scoped manifests for two sample tenants.
- KV cache: items are primarily in-memory and evicted by LRU/TTL. For certain debug scenarios we may persist compacted traces to a secured S3 bucket for up to 7 days; those are included in the manifest traces and can be redacted.
- Keystore: default is AWS KMS (customer can bring their own CMK); residency is configurable per-deployment region. Rotation is automated with rotation logs retained in our compliance S3 bucket. The matrix explains locations.
- SOC 2 / CAIQ artifacts: we can deliver the following by Dec 10 if that works: signed attestation (legal), two redacted deletion manifests, CloudTrail snippets showing DeleteObject events, and a short procedures doc for keystore rotation.

Would you prefer the signed attestation as a DocuSign envelope or an exported PDF? If you confirm Dec 10 for delivery we'll route legal/ops and include the manifests.

Links: Drive exhibit folder (restricted) — https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-exhibit-pack
DocuSign (placeholder) — https://app.docusign.com/prepare/12345-attenstion-request

If helpful I can loop Markus for the technical proof-of-delete extracts — cc'd. I'm available for the call Thu or Fri morning PT.

Best,

On Tue, Dec 1, 2026 at 10:03 AM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Elena —
> 
> Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a short checklist and our keystore residency matrix to start (see attachments). Quick summary here so your GRC team can triage:

Hi Elena / Priyom — adding a few technical clarifications and the location of the evidence extracts: 

1) Session deletion workflow:
   - TTL-driven cleanup runs as an asynchronous job (delete-worker) across each tenant's storage slice. Jobs emit a deletion manifest (JSON) with: tenant_id, object_key, deleted_at, job_id, and reason.
   - Proof-of-delete: for S3-backed deployments we record the DeleteObject response along with the request ID and store that response in our compliance bucket: s3://redwood-compliance/proof-of-delete/{tenant}/{yyyyMMdd}/. Those records are immutable and retention-controlled.

2) KV-cache and ephemeral traces:
   - Primary KV cache is in-memory on inference nodes. Eviction is LRU by token-age + configured TTL (default 6 hours for hosted, 30 minutes for dedicated low-latency pools).
   - For debugging (rare), a compact trace is written and encrypted to a restricted S3 path for up to 7 days; traces contain only opaque cache handles (no raw prompt text).

3) Keystore residency & rotation:
   - Customer CMKs: we support AWS KMS (regional) and external HSMs for private deployments. The residency matrix attached shows region-to-keystore mapping.
   - Rotation logs: rotation actions are recorded in CloudTrail and mirrored to the compliance bucket. We can export the CloudTrail snippets for the last 90 days for the keys you specify.

Attachments included for Elena: engineer-deletion-manifest-sample.json (redacted), and an export README that shows how to verify DeleteObject responses with request IDs.

If you need per-tenant manifests for two sample tenants, call that out and we'll generate redacted copies. We can also produce a signed attestation (legal) confirming the deletion workflows and storage locations.

-Markus
Principal Systems Engineer
